Macrons

Consonantal i

Body, health & movement

be awake verb

also awake, are you awake?, wide awake, stay up all night, time to get up

classical

Traupman 35, 38

vigilō, vigilāre

verb, first conjugation

Examples

  • Etiam vigilās? — Vigilō.

    Are you awake yet? — I amPlaut. Most. 383, 373b

  • Tempus est surgere.

    Time to get upTraupman 35

  • Somnium malum erat; nunc vigilās, et ego hīc sum.

    It was a bad dream; now you’re awake, and I’m here.composed

Other words

  • pervigilāre — stay awake all night

    also used · classical · Traupman 56: noctem pervigilābam

See also sleepy, dream, very early, stretch, drag out of bed.

SourcesLewis & Short: vigilo · Lewis & Short: pervigilo

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): pp. 35, 38, 56.

Plautus from the Latinitas loci collections.
